evidence.observation: 架空菓庵 is a fictional traditional wagashi shop; its name is four kanji.
Seasonal jō-namagashi and dorayaki with tsubu-an cooked every morning, wrapped one at a time at a small shopfront (小さな店頭).
After the faithful v2 build the owner asked for a more premium feel and originality than a plain left-right split hero and two equal product cards.
evidence.source_label: Owner instruction in the Issue #117 session, 2026-10-24

references.observed_principle: 複数の縦長ページが、和文縦組み・小さな説明文・茶器の写真・余白の繰り返しを使う。
references.transferable_idea: Only the principle: a short Japanese heading set vertically beside horizontal facts changes the reading axis; no page, image or copy is reused.

references.observed_principle: 生成りの地色、濃茶の太いロゴタイプ、粒子を思わせるドット模様の抽象図形。
references.transferable_idea: Only the principle: a simple dot rhythm can be a brand's memory point when a fact supports it; that brand's logo and pattern are not imitated.

references.observed_principle: ごく淡いオフホワイト地、中央の大きなセリフ体ロゴと左寄りの小さな和文説明、点のようなスクロール指示。
references.transferable_idea: Only the principle: a near-white ground, one large serif name and small grouped facts read as quiet and premium without decoration.

references.observed_principle: 白い面と薄い緑、中央の縦方向の日本語説明、下部の茶葉・茶碗と小さな説明を整列した構図。
references.transferable_idea: Only the principle: a loud opening, a calm middle and a precise information part give a short page its rhythm.

decisions.choice: The four-kanji name stands as one tall vertical column on the right third; the approved dorayaki concept crop sits in a framed window on the left half with open ground between them; no button block, one hairline text link.
decisions.rationale: A four-kanji name is short enough to read top to bottom, and the owner asked for more than a left-right photo split, so the name becomes the vertical axis.

decisions.choice: The four-kanji name set vertically in a large Mincho as the one vertical accent; nav and facts stay small horizontal sans at a readable body size.
decisions.rationale: A short kanji name reads well top to bottom, while hours, address and phone must stay horizontal; only the name changes axis and grows.

decisions.choice: Kinari ground on most of the page, sumi text, and one deep azuki-plum used only for the dot mark and the active nav item; no filled red button.
decisions.rationale: The single accent comes from the azuki of the shop's own tsubu-an, and keeping it off large fills keeps the page quiet as the owner asked.

decisions.choice: At most two approved concept crops, never as equal cards: one large in the hero window, one small inset beside a verbatim description line; a short row of small round dots is the photo-free memory point.
decisions.rationale: The dots stand for the azuki grains of tsubu-an cooked every morning, a mark that exists only because of this shop's fact.

decisions.choice: Each section has a different lead: the vertical name in the hero, one verbatim description sentence set large in the middle, a narrow factual ledger last.
decisions.rationale: The description moves from the morning's tsubu-an to wrapping each sweet at the small shopfront, so the middle section is led by words, not a second image row.

decisions.choice: A thin horizontal header with the name and two anchors to the details and the shop information; nothing about ordering or reservations.
decisions.rationale: The fixture offers no ordering, so the header only reaches verified content and stays small beside a large vertical name.

decisions.choice: On a phone the name turns horizontal and large above the hero image; the dot mark, the description sentence and the ledger follow in one column.
decisions.rationale: A vertical name in a 390px column would crowd the image, and the whole four-kanji name has to be read before anything decorative.

decisions.choice: Within the current comp-impl CSS allowlist: the vertical name as a one-character-wide box (no writing-mode), dots as small rounded boxes, no gradients or overlapping layers; keep a header, three sections and a ledger.
decisions.rationale: v1 (photo-free, poster-like) failed as a web page; keeping a real header, sections and ledger avoids that, and the allowlist needs no new approval.
